name: English bespoke tailoring
summary: The cut of the London tailor: a plain, dark suit in fine worsted, drafted for one body and built by hand on hair canvas.

philosophy.core_thesis: A man's suit is drafted for one body, built inside with canvas, and shown outside by a plain surface and a line with no fuss.
design_principles: Draft the pattern from 20 or more measures, and cut it by hand from a single length of cloth.
Baste a first fitting, then a forward fitting, then a finished fitting; allow 50 or more hours of work for a suit.
Build the chest on a canvas of horsehair and wool, pad-stitched by hand to hold the roll of the lapel.
Cut the coat with a clean chest and a gentle drape, and a waist that is lightly suppressed.
Set the sleeve head with a small roped or natural edge; sew the buttonholes by hand.
Choose a dark, plain cloth of 280 to 400 g per metre: navy, charcoal, grey.
Keep the trousers high at the waist, with pleats, a straight leg and a turn-up.
anti_patterns: A boxy, ready-made block with no fitting
Glued fusible interlining in the chest
Padded, square shoulders with a hard edge

silhouette.shape: A long, balanced line: a clean chest, a soft shoulder, a lightly shaped waist and a straight leg.
silhouette.line: The lapel rolls in one curve to the first button; the back hangs without a ripple; the trouser falls straight to a light break.
silhouette.fit: Close on the chest and the shoulder, with room at the arm and the seat, so that the wearer can move.
silhouette.proportion: Jacket length covers the seat; lapel about 8 to 10 cm; trouser rise about 30 cm; sleeve shows 1 cm of shirt cuff.
rules: Fit the shoulder first; the rest of the coat hangs from it.
Roll the lapel by hand, and do not press it flat.
Cut the back with a centre seam and a vent or two side vents, so that it sits flat.
Pair a dark coat with a plain waistcoat or a light shirt; keep the colour low.
Match the stripe or the check at each seam.

fabrics.rule: Choose a fine wool with a close twill: worsted for town, flannel and tweed for the country, canvas inside and silk twill for the lining.

methods: pattern drafted to the measures of one client
hair canvas pad-stitched to the chest
shoulder and sleeve head set by hand
construction.closures: A two- or three-button front in horn or corozo; four buttons at the sleeve that open; a fly front on the trousers.
construction.details: Notch or peak lapel, flap pockets, a ticket pocket, a vent or two, cuff buttons that open, and a lining in silk twill.

surface.pattern: Plain cloth, or a discreet stripe, check or herringbone; the pattern is matched at each seam.
surface.gloss: Worsted at 3–8 GU; the cloth stays matte, with a soft face from the press.
surface.wear: A good suit improves with wear: the canvas takes the shape of the body, and the tailor can let out, take in and re-press.

palette.strategy: Dark, quiet town colours; softer browns and greens in tweed for the country.

processes: cutting by hand from a drafted pattern
canvas and pad stitching by hand
hand finish of buttonholes and lining
making.scale: Bespoke: one suit for one client, with three fittings, by a cutter and a team of coat, trouser and waistcoat makers.
making.signs: Hand pick-stitch at the lapel edge, a lapel that rolls, a lining that is hand-felled, and buttonholes cut and sewn by hand.

pieces.form: Single-breasted, two-button jacket with a rolled lapel
High-waisted pleated trousers with a straight leg
Five-button waistcoat with a shaped back
Chesterfield overcoat with a velvet collar
Poplin shirt with a cut-away collar

canonical_works.work: Dinner jacket for the Prince of Wales

emotion.target_response: A sense of calm authority: the viewer sees a clean line and a fine cloth and reads care and trust.

use_cases: a brief for a made-to-measure menswear label
a period costume brief for a Victorian or Edwardian gentleman
a fashion image prompt for a tailor's atelier
a study note on the history of the suit
avoid_when: the brief is casual or sportswear
the brief wants stretch or technical cloth
the brief is a ready-to-wear mass line

modifiers.how: Drop the shoulder padding, cut a straight sack body, and use a button-down shirt.
Widen the shoulder, deepen the chalk stripe, and cut the waist close.

ornament_level.note: The suit is plain; a lining, a button or a pocket square carries the colour.
